The rule also applies when moving the other way around: the king moves two squares away from the castle's square but does not land on any piece that would put it in check. Similarly, the rook moves straight over the square in front of it without landing on any piece that would put it in check.

This move is considered legal if both kings are on different sides of the board and neither has any pieces on the same file as the attacking piece (king for castling) or the defending piece (rook for castling).
